summary: feat(pagination): capture the Fiken-Api-* result-count headers and use them for provenance, a sync completeness check and doctor (issue #15)
reason: Fiken's list endpoints answer with a bare JSON array and no envelope, so the only completeness signal on the wire is the response header block Fiken-Api-Page / -Page-Size / -Page-Count / -Result-Count (spec.yaml:247-255, declared on 27 of the 40 list operations). The printed client discarded resp.Header except Content-Type, so nothing - not sync, not doctor, not a paginated read's provenance envelope - could tell how many rows a resource holds or whether a page was the last one. That is why issue #12 (the page-1 skip that landed 477 of 577 accounts) went unnoticed for the life of the mirror. The capture is a context-value sink in the hand-authored internal/client/page_info.go (PageInfo, PageInfoSink, NewPageInfoContext, ParsePageInfo, GetPage) so the generated request path needs exactly one line - capturePageInfo(ctx, resp.Header) in the success branch of (*Client).doInternal - and no signature anywhere changes: paginatedGet and its 27 generated call sites, and both sync walkers' `c.Get` interface, are untouched. The sink keeps the FIRST response that carried headers (Result-Count is the collection total on every page) and Reset starts a new collection. Consumers: (1) resolvePaginatedReadWithStrategy installs a sink and each live return passes the provenance through attachPageInfo, which fills the new optional DataProvenance.ResultCount/PageCount pointers; wrapWithProvenance emits meta.result_count and meta.page_count only when present, so an absent header is never published as a zero count. (2) syncResource and syncDependentResource compare the rows they landed against Fiken-Api-Result-Count and emit one sync_anomaly with reason result_count_mismatch per (company, resource) when they differ; the comparison is skipped for a walk that was resumed from a stored cursor or exited early (--max-pages / --latest-only, stuck cursor, non-JSON body, fetch or upsert error), because such a walk is short by construction and says nothing about completeness. (3) sync_state gains a nullable result_count column (declared in the CREATE for a fresh DB and in backfillColumns for an existing one - backfillColumns runs before the CREATE statements, so a fresh DB needs both) written by the new SaveSyncResultCount and read by SyncResultCount, and doctor's cache report adds result_count to a resource entry when one was recorded. The recorded number is only written when it is on the same scale as sync_state.total_count, which is the mirror-wide row count (syncStateTotalCount): headers present for every parent walked, no early exit, and no --company scope. A --company or capped run leaves the previously recorded value alone rather than overwriting it with a partial sum. NULL result_count means 'no run ever saw the header', which is not the same claim as zero rows - hence PageInfo.Present / HasResultCount and the *int provenance fields.

validated_outcome: make check green (go vet ./..., go test ./..., scripts/check-boundaries.sh). Hand-authored tests: internal/client/page_info_test.go drives an httptest server that sets the four headers - TestGetPage_ParsesFikenPaginationHeaders parses {0 100 3 250} alongside the body, TestGetPage_NoHeadersIsAbsentNotZero keeps a header-less response at the zero value, TestPageInfoSink_KeepsFirstResponseAndResets pins first-page-wins and Reset, TestPageInfoSink_NilAndUnsetContextAreNoOps keeps the patched doInternal line harmless without a sink. internal/cli/pagination_headers_test.go extends the pageServer harness from pagination_zero_based_test.go with the header block: meta.result_count/page_count appear on a paginated read (single page and --all) and are omitted without headers; a pull of 150 rows against a claimed Result-Count of 250 emits exactly one result_count_mismatch (result_count 250, rows 150) on both the flat and the dependent walker, a complete 250-row pull emits none and records 250, a --max-pages 1 walk emits none and records nothing, and doctor's cache report shows result_count for a resource that has one and omits it for one that does not (HOME redirected to a temp dir so the real mirror is untouched). No live API call was made.
